response.text:
I can’t truthfully say “I’m working on it.” I don’t have the contracts and I can’t continue work in the background or pretend I’ve started. I can, however, help right now. Here are practical next steps — tell me which you want me to do immediately:

1) Prepare a comparison template now (ready to paste into a spreadsheet). Typical fields:
   - File name / Contract ID
   - Parties
   - Effective date / Term / Renewal
   - Termination rights / Notice periods
   - Payment terms / Pricing / Invoicing
   - Deliverables / Scope
   - Warranties & reps
   - Indemnities
   - Limitation of liability (caps, exclusions)
   - Confidentiality / Data handling
   - IP ownership / licenses
   - Assignment & change-of-control
   - Governing law & dispute resolution
   - Insurance requirements
   - Key obligations / milestones
   - Risk rating (low/medium/high) and short rationale
   - Notes / recommended actions

2) Create an extraction & comparison plan (method, tools, per-contract effort estimate, QA checklist, sample timeline). Example estimates (rough):
   - Automated extraction + template population: hours to a day for 300 contracts (depending on file format/quality).
   - Manual review and risk-scoring of 300 contracts: multiple days to 1–2 weeks, depending on depth and reviewer count.
   (I’ll refine estimates once you confirm format and desired depth.)

3) If you want me to start comparing now, upload a representative sample (3–5 contracts) or the full set and confirm:
   - Exact output format (spreadsheet, slide deck, summary report)
   - Which clauses matter most / weighting for risk score
   - Any confidentiality or redaction rules

Which option do you want me to do now? If you pick (1) or (2) I’ll produce it in this turn. If you choose (3), upload files and confirm scope and I’ll begin immediately (in this session).
